subject: Business
title: The Power of Starting Early
description: A 60-second lesson on The Power of Starting Early.

hook.text: Alice invests $200/month from age 25 to 35 and stops. Bob invests $200/month from age 35 to 65. Alice ends with more.

buildup.text: Starting early gives compound interest more time to work. Each extra year at the beginning matters enormously.

discovery.text: Alice invested $24,000 total. Bob invested $72,000 total. But Alice's 10 extra years of compounding beat Bob's 30 years.

twist.text: Young people often say they'll invest 'later when they earn more.' But delaying 10 years can cost $500,000+ by retirement.

climax.text: The best financial decision a 22-year-old can make isn't a high salary. It's investing consistently from day one.

punchline.text: The best time to invest was yesterday. The second best time is today.

quiz.question: Why does Alice end up wealthier despite investing less money than Bob?
options: Her 10 extra years of compounding outweigh Bob's larger total contributions

details.summary: Starting to invest early gives compound interest maximum time to work, creating an exponential advantage that cannot be replicated by starting later with more money. A 25-year-old investing modestly will typically outperform a 35-year-old investing aggressively.
details.whyItMatters: The biggest investing advantage anyone can have is time. Demonstrating that early small amounts beat later large amounts motivates young people to start immediately, even with modest sums.
takeaways: Ten extra years of compounding typically doubles the final investment value
Starting small is far better than waiting until you can afford to invest more
The cost of waiting increases exponentially with each year delayed

faq.question: How much does delaying investment by ten years actually cost?
faq.answer: Investing 300 dollars monthly starting at age 25 at 8 percent returns yields about 1 million dollars by age 65. Starting the same amount at 35 yields only about 440,000 dollars. The ten-year delay costs over 560,000 dollars, more than the total contributions.

faq.question: What if you genuinely cannot afford to invest in your twenties?
faq.answer: Even 25 or 50 dollars monthly gets compounding started. Many brokerages have no minimums. The habit of investing matters as much as the amount. When income increases, you can raise contributions, but the early small amounts will have had the longest time to grow.
